record:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Aurora Search Labs building enterprise semantic search product (doc indexing + hybrid retrieval + reranking). Heavy focus on latency and unit economics. They already run their own retrieval stack; looking to standardize LLM inference + reranking with predictable SLOs.
- Key theme: they will not allow automated cost optimizations to impact relevance without enforced, measurable guardrails.

FIRMOGRAPHICS / ENV
- HQ: US (remote team; some customers in EU).
- Deployment preference: VPC / isolated networking for production. Will accept Hosted API for quick POC as long as a path to Dedicated/VPC is clear.
- Data handling: customer documents may contain sensitive content; wants explicit retention controls + auditability.

USE CASES (CURRENT + PLANNED)
- Primary: embeddings + reranking. Secondary: summarization of search results / snippet generation.
- Traffic shape (POC estimates):
  - Embeddings: high volume batch (indexing) + moderate QPS online.
  - Reranking: low latency, online path.
- Model behavior sensitivity:
  - Reranker quality changes are very noticeable in user relevance metrics.
  - For generation (snippets), they can tolerate minor stylistic drift but not factual regressions.

LATENCY / THROUGHPUT / COST NOTES
- Target SLOs (stated on calls; not yet contract language):
  - Reranking p95 <= 120ms (end-to-end service time goal).
  - Embedding online p95 <= 80ms.
- Cost: explicit goal to reduce per-query cost; currently over budget when reranking is enabled for most queries.
- They are interested in Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profiles) but only if changes are gated and traceable.

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS
- Must-have: SOC 2 report, SSO/SAML, audit logging, configurable retention, KMS integration.
- Security quote (paraphrased): "We need proof that no one can click a button and silently change model behavior in prod." They asked how Redwood prevents accidental regressions during cost optimization.
- They reacted positively to: mandatory quality gates before applying Optimize recommendations + audit trail for approvals/overrides.

QUALITY GUARDRAILS / PROCUREMENT CONFIDENCE (KEY THREAD)
- Procurement concern: Optimize is attractive, but they see it as a risk surface unless there are hard controls.
- What moved the deal forward:
  - Defense-in-depth enforcement (Optimize apply boundary + rollout controller promotion checks).
  - Gate run artifacts + deltas vs baseline exposed in Console.
  - Override mechanics: time-bound, explicit owner, reason required, audit events.
- Ask from Aurora: include this in a written security addendum / Q&A (not just verbal).

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2026-02-06 Fireflies: Security review deep dive ("quality gates and audit trail"). Attendees: Aurora Security + Eng; Redwood: Diego Ramos (SE), Aditya Rao (PM Optimize), Marcus Lin (security review). Outcome: security requested written answers on enforcement points + override RBAC.
- 2026-02-11 Internal: SE noted they are more likely to pick Dedicated if we can commit to consistent p95 and isolation; Hosted OK for POC.
- 2026-02-20 Fireflies: POC check-in ("cost savings with quality gates"). Aurora wants to see (1) gate pass rate stability, (2) what happens on gate failures (block apply + rollback), (3) expected runtime/cost of running gates.
- 2026-02-27 Email: Aurora procurement asked whether gating is available for quantization profile switches specifically (they are most concerned about this category). Responded: yes, quant profile changes require gates; overrides are time-bounded and audited.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Confirm whether they need EU-only processing for certain tenants (data residency). If yes: region strategy + gate execution capacity in-region.
- Clarify which routes are considered "production" during POC; they want gating even for limited production trials.

RISKS
- If gate runtime is too slow (blocks rollouts), they may disable Optimize entirely and revert to manual tuning.
- If gates are flaky (false positives), trust will be reduced; they asked for a quarantine / rerun policy for flaky suites.

PROPOSED NEXT STEPS
1) Send 1-pager: "How Optimize Quality Gates Work" (enforcement points, artifacts, override policy, audit exports).
2) Dedicated sizing + architecture call for VPC deployment (include expected throughput, model families, regions).
3) Define POC success criteria with Aurora PM: relevance metric thresholds + latency/cost targets; map to gate tiers (smoke vs full gates).
